Kara is training for the swim leg of a triathlon and decides to go for a training swim in the harbour. She starts at a jetty $J$ and swims on a bearing of 105° for 0.9 km out to a buoy $L$. She then changes direction and swims on a bearing of 045° for a further 1.6 km to buoy $M$ before returning to the jetty $J$.

What is the total distance that Kara swam, correct to 2 decimal places?
questions.answer:
At $L$, the bearing back to $J$ is $285^\circ$ and the new bearing is $045^\circ$, so $\angle JLM = 285^\circ - 45^\circ = 240^\circ$ reflex, i.e. $120^\circ$ inside the triangle.
$$JM^2 = 0.9^2 + 1.6^2 - 2(0.9)(1.6)\cos 120^\circ = 4.81 \Rightarrow JM \approx 2.193\text{ km}$$
$$\text{Total} = 0.9 + 1.6 + 2.193 \approx 4.69\text{ km}$$
(The school's sheet gives no worked answer for this part.)

$$\frac{\sin\angle JML}{0.9} = \frac{\sin 120^\circ}{2.193} \Rightarrow \angle JML \approx 20.8^\circ$$

$$225^\circ + 20.8^\circ \approx 246^\circ$$

questions.question:
A company is designing a water bottle with the shape below as its cross-section. It consists of an isosceles triangle with a base 10 cm and a semicircle with a diameter that fits perfectly to one equal side of the isosceles triangle. The area of the triangle is 60 cm².

If the bottle is to have a depth of 25 cm, calculate the volume of the bottle to two decimal places.
questions.answer:
Triangle height: $60 = \frac12 \times 10 \times h \Rightarrow h = 12$ cm.

questions.answer:

City $H$ is 860 km from city $G$ on a bearing of $110^\circ$. City $F$ is 730 km due south of city $G$.

Find the distance, correct to the nearest km, and the bearing, correct to the nearest degree, of city $F$ from city $H$.
questions.answer:
$\angle FGH = 180^\circ - 110^\circ = 70^\circ$.

**Distance** (cosine rule):
$$FH^2 = 860^2 + 730^2 - 2(860)(730)\cos 70^\circ \approx 843\,059 \Rightarrow FH \approx 918\text{ km}$$

**Angle at $H$** (sine rule):
$$\frac{\sin \angle GHF}{730} = \frac{\sin 70^\circ}{918.18} \Rightarrow \angle GHF \approx 48.3^\circ$$

**Bearing:** the bearing of $G$ from $H$ is $110^\circ + 180^\circ = 290^\circ$. $F$ is $48.3^\circ$ anticlockwise from that direction:
$$290^\circ - 48.3^\circ \approx 242^\circ$$

$F$ is about **918 km from $H$ on a bearing of $242^\circ$**.

questions.answer:
$\angle QPR = 80^\circ - 55^\circ = 25^\circ$. Sine rule:
$$\frac{\sin\angle QRP}{12} = \frac{\sin 25^\circ}{8.5} \implies \sin\angle QRP = 0.5966\ldots$$

questions.answer:
$\angle PQR = 180^\circ - 25^\circ - 143^\circ 22' = 11^\circ 38'$.

The bearing of $P$ from $R$ is $080^\circ + 180^\circ = 260^\circ$. With the obtuse angle at $R$, $R$ is only about 4 km from $P$ and $Q$ lies to the north-east of $R$, so turning clockwise from $RP$ through $143^\circ 22'$:
$$260^\circ + 143^\circ 22' - 360^\circ = 43^\circ 22'.$$
The bearing of $Q$ from $R$ is about **043°T**.

Six towns are linked by a road network. Two of the towns have roads leading directly to three other towns, while all the other towns have roads leading directly to two other towns.

- From town $Q$, roads lead to towns $P$, $R$ and $S$.

Which of the following network diagrams could represent the positions of towns $P$ and $T$ on the road network linking the six towns?
questions.answer:
$P$ has degree 2 and one of its neighbours, $Q$, has degree 3 (joined to $P$, $R$, $S$), so $T$ cannot be adjacent to $P$ or $Q$.
- (A): $T$ is joined to the degree-3 vertex next to $P$, which must be $Q$, but $Q$ is not joined to $T$.
- (B): $T$ is joined to $P$, but $P$ only leads to $Q$ and $U$.
- (C): $P$ has degree 3.
- (D): $P$ (degree 2) is joined to $U$ and to the degree-3 vertex $Q$, which leads on to $R$ and $S$; $T$ fits. **(D)**

The formulas below are used to calculate an estimate for blood alcohol content (BAC) for females and males respectively.
$$\text{BAC}_{\text{female}} = \frac{10N - 7.5H}{5.5M} \qquad \text{BAC}_{\text{male}} = \frac{10N - 7.5H}{6.8M}$$
where $N$ is the number of standard drinks consumed, $H$ is the number of hours of drinking and $M$ is the person's weight in kilograms.

Juliana and Donald go to a party together and both start drinking at 8.30 pm. The party ends at 1.30 am. At this point Donald and Juliana have the same BAC.

Donald is male, weighs 73 kilograms and drank 4 full-strength beers during the party. Each full-strength beer is equivalent to 1.4 standard drinks.

Juliana is female, weighs 51 kilograms and drank low-strength beer. Each low-strength beer is equivalent to 0.8 standard drinks.

How many low-strength beers did Juliana drink during the party? Answer correct to the nearest whole number.
questions.answer:
$H = 5$ hours. Donald: $N = 4 \times 1.4 = 5.6$.
$$\text{BAC} = \frac{10(5.6) - 7.5(5)}{6.8 \times 73} = \frac{18.5}{496.4} \approx 0.037268$$
Juliana, with $N$ standard drinks:
$$\frac{10N - 37.5}{5.5 \times 51} = 0.037268 \Rightarrow 10N - 37.5 \approx 10.454 \Rightarrow N \approx 4.795$$
Number of low-strength beers $= \dfrac{4.795}{0.8} \approx 6$.

Sierra has saved up a deposit of \$60 000 and will take out a mortgage from the bank for the balance at an interest rate of 6% per annum, compounding monthly. Her parents have agreed to cover any other costs of the purchase.

| Years | 2% | 4% | 6% | 8% | 10% |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| 15 | 155.3981 | 135.1921 | 118.5035 | 104.6406 | 93.0574 |
| 20 | 197.6740 | 165.0219 | 139.5808 | 119.5543 | 103.6246 |
| 25 | 235.9301 | 189.4525 | 155.2069 | 129.5645 | 110.0472 |

questions.answer:
Loan $= 1\,000\,000 - 60\,000 = \$940\,000$.

- Years 11–30 at \$7000: $7000 \times (166.7916 - 90.0735) = \$537\,026.70$

questions.answer:
Each boy wins one game: Thomas then Max, or Max then Thomas.

questions.question:
A ball is thrown vertically upwards from a balcony and its height $h$ metres above the ground over time $t$ seconds is modelled using the equation $h = -5t^2 + 10t + 40$. The graph of $h$ against $t$ is shown.

The equation $h = -5t^2 + 10t + 40$ only models the flight of the ball for some values of $t$. Explain which values are invalid and why.
questions.answer:
- $t < 0$: time cannot be negative (before the ball is thrown).
- $t > 4$: the ball hits the ground at $t = 4$ ($h = 0$); after that the model gives negative heights, i.e. below the ground, which is impossible.

The model is only valid for $0 \le t \le 4$.

questions.answer:
Median \$510; $Q_1 = \$350$, $Q_3 = \$610$, so $\text{IQR} = 260$.

questions.question:
A compass radial survey of the field $ABCD$ has been conducted from a central point $O$. The readings are: $A$ on a bearing of 310°, $OA = 85$ m; $B$ on 021°, $OB = 64$ m; $D$ on 256°, $OD = 70$ m; $OC = 52$ m.

Farmer Tran wants to fence around the area $ABOD$. Find the cost of this project if each metre of fencing costs \$22.
questions.answer:
$\angle AOB = 360^\circ - 310^\circ + 21^\circ = 71^\circ$ and $\angle AOD = 310^\circ - 256^\circ = 54^\circ$.
$$AB^2 = 85^2 + 64^2 - 2(85)(64)\cos 71^\circ \implies AB \approx 88.20 \text{ m}$$
$$AD^2 = 85^2 + 70^2 - 2(85)(70)\cos 54^\circ \implies AD \approx 71.63 \text{ m}$$
Perimeter of $ABOD = 88.20 + 64 + 70 + 71.63 \approx 293.82$ m. Cost $\approx 293.82 \times 22 = \$6464.13$.

The surveyor finds that the area of triangle $BOC$ is $1664\ \text{m}^2$. Find the bearing of $C$ from $O$.
questions.answer:
$\frac12 \times 64 \times 52 \times \sin\angle BOC = 1664 \implies \sin\angle BOC = 1 \implies \angle BOC = 90^\circ$.

Bearing of $C$ from $O$ $= 21^\circ + 90^\circ = 111^\circ$T.

questions.question:
Track works are required across the Sydney rail network and 13 activities are needed to be completed. The network diagram shows these activities, including their completion times in weeks: $A$ (6) and $B$ (3) start the project; $C$ (2) follows $B$; $D$ (3) and $E$ (5) follow $A$ and $C$; $F$ (5) follows $B$; $G$ (4) follows $D$; $H$ (2), $I$ (2) and $J$ (3) follow $E$; $L$ (5) follows $G$ and $H$; $K$ (3) follows $F$ and $J$; $M$ (1) follows $I$ and $L$. The project finishes after $K$ and $M$.

The project currently takes 19 weeks. The contractor proposes a reduction in completion time for activities $A$, $E$, $F$ and $L$, at an additional cost. The table below summarises these costs. Each activity can only be reduced by a maximum of three weeks.

| Activity | Weekly cost (\$) |
|---|---|
| $A$ | 130 000 |
| $E$ | 110 000 |
| $F$ | 120 000 |
| $L$ | 100 000 |

If the overall completion time for the project can be reduced to 15 weeks, find the minimum cost of this change. Your answer should explain clearly why the minimum cost is achieved.
questions.answer:
Every path must end up at most 15 weeks. Let $a$, $e$, $l$ be the reductions of $A$, $E$, $L$ ($F$ is on no long path, so reducing it does not help).

| Path | Length | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| $A$–$D$–$G$–$L$–$M$ | 19 | $a + l \ge 4$ |
| $A$–$E$–$H$–$L$–$M$ | 19 | $a + e + l \ge 4$ |
| $B$–$C$–$D$–$G$–$L$–$M$ | 18 | $l \ge 3$ |
| $B$–$C$–$E$–$H$–$L$–$M$ | 18 | $e + l \ge 3$ |
| $A$–$E$–$J$–$K$ | 17 | $a + e \ge 2$ |
| $B$–$C$–$E$–$J$–$K$ | 16 | $e \ge 1$ |

$B$–$C$–$D$–$G$–$L$–$M$ forces $l = 3$ (the maximum), so $a + l \ge 4$ forces $a \ge 1$; $B$–$C$–$E$–$J$–$K$ forces $e \ge 1$. Taking $a = 1$, $e = 1$, $l = 3$ meets every condition:
$$\text{Minimum cost} = 130\,000 + 110\,000 + 3 \times 100\,000 = \$540\,000.$$

(The paper's sample answer gives \$430 000 by reducing only $A$ and $L$, but that leaves $A$–$E$–$J$–$K$ at 16 weeks and $B$–$C$–$E$–$J$–$K$ at 16 weeks, so the project would still take 16 weeks.)
